Dr Michael Biggs
Neurologist
North Shore Private Hospital
3 Westbourne St
St Leonards NWS

06 April 2018

Dear Dr Biggs

Re: Mr Chadwick Hooper
DOB: 26/01/1993

I am writing to refer Mr Hooper, a 25-year-old bartender whose clinical features are suggestive of an intracranial space occupying lesion, for urgent management in the emergency department.

Today, Mr Hooper was found fallen at his home after experiencing a severe left sided headache, right sided parathesia, slurred speech, along with altered level of consciousness for the last three hours. He had an increased right knee jerk, and his BP was 155/90. However, his PR and reflexes were normal.

The symptoms first occurred on 13/02/2018 when Mr Hooper presented with a frontal headache, blurred vision and nausea. At that time, his examination was unremarkable. Therefore, he was prescribed paracetamol every four hours and advised to take adequate rest. 

Despite the treatment, Mr Hopper’s condition further deteriorated. Two weeks later, the headache became more severe and throbbing in nature. His BP was 160/95. Consequently, pethidine and intramuscular maxolone were administered. Since then, he has been stable until today.

Mr Hooper smokes 2-3 cigarettes per day and drinks heavily but does not use any illicit drugs. He has no drug allergies. His family history is positive for hypertension. 

Given the above, I would greatly appreciate your timely assessment and management of Mr Hooper at your earlist convenience.

Please do not hesitate to contact me if you require any further information.

Yours sincerely

Doctor.
